title: Bounded site comparison of compositor and refinement conjugates
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum [def-pur-conventions]: $k$ is an algebraic closure of a finite field of characteristic $p$, $\ell\ne p$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite, $n\ge1$ and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. All schemes are finite-type $k$-schemes and every morphism to which compact support is applied is separated and finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. No absolute separatedness is assumed. For each such $h:S\to T$ choose $c_h=(j_h:S\hookrightarrow\overline S,r_h:\overline S\to T)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], put $C_V=\nu_V^*$ [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], $F_h^e=Rr_{h,e,*}j_{h,!}^e$ and $F_h^p=Rr_{h,p,*}j_{h,!}^p$. Use the specified proper-mate/open comparison $B_h:C_TF_h^e\xrightarrow{\sim}F_h^pC_S$ [lem-pur-compact-support-site-coherence], the ordinary etale right adjoint $G_h^e$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], the transported $G_h^p=Rh^!$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and their counits $\varepsilon_h^e,\varepsilon_h^p$. Write $a_{h,L}=\rho_L:C_SG_h^eL\xrightarrow{\sim}G_h^pC_TL$ for the comparison induced by the site-adjunction unit, with the bounded-origin Hom normalization of [lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose]. Only bounded-below etale inputs, bounded-below exceptional images, and bounded-below intermediate etale objects of the displayed composites are used; all pro-etale exceptional Hom bijections are the bounded etale-origin ones.

Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be composable, $h=g\circ f$, with compatible chosen compactification towers. Let $\alpha^\sigma:F_g^\sigma F_f^\sigma\to F_h^\sigma$ be their specified compact-support compositors, $\sigma=e,p$, and let $t^\sigma:G_h^\sigma\to G_f^\sigma G_g^\sigma$ be their right-adjoint conjugates [def-pur-chosen-compactification-compositors, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], using the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Explicitly, $t^\sigma_K$ is the transpose under $F_g^\sigma F_f^\sigma\dashv G_f^\sigma G_g^\sigma$ of $\varepsilon^\sigma_{h,K}\circ\alpha^\sigma_{G_h^\sigma K}$. Then
$$ (G_f^p(a_{g,K}))\circ a_{f,G_g^eK}\circ C_X(t^e_K)
=t^p_{C_ZK}\circ a_{h,K}. $$
For two compactifications $c,c'$ of $f$ and a specified proper refinement, let $r^\sigma:F_f^{\sigma,c}\to F_f^{\sigma,c'}$ be its specified comparison and $q^\sigma:G_f^{\sigma,c'}\to G_f^{\sigma,c}$ its conjugate. Then
$$a^c_{f,K}\circ C_X(q^e_K)=q^p_{C_YK}\circ a^{c'}_{f,K}.$$
Both equalities hold for every $K$ for which the bounded-below inputs and intermediate exceptional images specified above exist. They identify the actual chosen arrows, preserve identity comparisons, and commute with every further compatible composition or refinement: the comparison of a pasted left-adjoint diagram has as its conjugate the corresponding pasted right-adjoint diagram, with the canonical composite-adjunction associators inserted. No tensor projection, Cartesian exchange, smoothness or purity assertion is included.

proof.text: Each chosen Stage already carries its finite nonnegative dimension bound, including the empty-scheme case. Apply the isomorphism clause of [lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose] with that bound to construct the specified rho comparison. For a single stage, expand the normalized boundedSiteTranspose: the inverse compact-support site comparison composed with the inverse boundary component is C of the inverse bounded-to-ambient etale compatibility. Naturality of the comparison-adjunction unit and target naturality of the ordinary etale Hom bijection then identify the transpose of B inverse followed by C(z) with C of the ordinary etale transpose followed by rho. This uses the specified unit and boundary, with no ambient pro-etale exceptional adjunction.

source.place: Tags 0B65 and 0DV0; explicit bounded-origin Hom-bijection calculation

proof.text: Prove source and target naturality of the recursive ordinary etale Hom bijections by induction on a word, starting with ordinary adjunction naturality and the bounded-to-ambient compatibility. Prove target naturality of the recursive pro-etale transpose similarly. Induct on a parenthesized word W to obtain transpose_W(B_W inverse followed by C(z)) = C(homEquiv_W(z)) followed by rho_W for every bounded etale source J, admissible etale target K, and z : F_W^e J to K. At a composite first use the last-word formula, cancel the mapped first-word boundary with its inverse, use target naturality to move the last rho through the first transpose, and apply the first-word formula. This is the order of the composite Hom bijection in [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. All required intermediate bounds are projections of Word.Admissible.

source.place: Tags 0B65 and 0DV0; explicit bounded-origin Hom-bijection calculation

proof.text: Induct on the left-pasting syntax to prove C(etaleMap_D) followed by B_V = B_U followed by proMap_D. The refinement and compositor cases are exactly the specified squares of [lem-pur-compact-support-site-coherence]. Vertical composition uses functoriality. Before-whiskering cancels the inserted boundary and its inverse; after-whiskering uses boundary naturality. Identity, associator and unitor components are identities. Apply the word transpose formula to etaleMap_D followed by the target-word counit; this square identifies the two inputs of the transpose. Consequently C(etaleConjugate_D) followed by rho_U = rho_V followed by proConjugate_D.

source.place: Tags 0B65 and 0DV0; explicit bounded-origin Hom-bijection calculation

proof.text: Define a private recursively pasted etale right arrow: use etaleConjugate for primitive refinements/compositors, reverse vertical composition, apply the first right functor for before-whiskering, evaluate at the last right image for after-whiskering, and use identities for unitors and associators. First prove for any z : F_V^e J to K that homEquiv_U(etaleMap_D followed by z) = homEquiv_V(z) followed by this recursive right arrow. For a primitive diagram this follows by expressing z as the target counit precomposed with the image of its transpose, then using naturality of etaleMap_D and source naturality of homEquiv. Induct on pastings: the vertical case applies the two induction hypotheses; the two whiskering cases use target and source naturality respectively; associators merely reassociate the same Hom-equivalence functions. At z equal to the target counit, its transpose is identity, so etaleConjugate_D equals the recursively pasted etale right arrow.

source.place: Tags 0B65 and 0DV0; explicit bounded-origin Hom-bijection calculation

proof.text: Prove naturality of rho_W by induction on words; the single-stage case is naturality of the site-adjunction unit, and the composite case uses functoriality and both induction hypotheses. Compare the recursive etale and pro-etale pasted right arrows by induction on D. Primitive cases are the conjugate comparison proved above. The vertical case uses the two comparisons and functoriality. Before-whiskering uses rho naturality for the first word and the induction hypothesis for D. After-whiskering uses the induction hypothesis at the last etale exceptional image, then cancels the last rho with its inverse under the first right functor. Identity, associator and unitor cases reduce to identity components and functoriality. Thus C of the recursive etale right arrow followed by rho_U equals rho_V followed by rightMap_D.

source.place: Tags 0B65 and 0DV0; explicit bounded-origin Hom-bijection calculation

proof.text: Replace the recursive etale right arrow by etaleConjugate_D in the comparison of the preceding step. This proves the second asserted conjunct. Compare it with the entire-conjugate equation from the left site square and cancel the invertible rho_V on the left; this gives proConjugate_D = rightMap_D, the first conjunct. Every boundedness hypothesis used was one of Word.Admissible or Paste.IntermediateBounds. No tensor, Cartesian exchange, smoothness or purity assertion is used.
